name: Manthali
blurb: A small airstrip in Ramechhap district, four to five hours' drive east of Kathmandu. In the busy spring and autumn months most Lukla flights leave from here instead of the capital.
tip: Flights leave soon after dawn, so most people drive out from Kathmandu around 1 am or sleep in Manthali the night before.

name: Lukla
blurb: The gateway to Khumbu, built around the short, sloping runway of Tenzing-Hillary Airport. Guides and porters meet their groups here and the trail north begins at the edge of the village.
tip: Keep one spare day in your schedule for flight delays, especially on the way out.

name: Phakding
blurb: A riverside lodge village on the Dudh Koshi, lower than Lukla, where most trekkers spend their first night.

name: Monjo
blurb: The last village before the Sagarmatha National Park gate, where park and municipality permits are checked. A quieter place to sleep than Phakding if you want a shorter climb to Namche.

name: Namche Bazaar
blurb: The Sherpa capital, set in a steep horseshoe bowl above the Bhote Koshi. It is the last place with real shops, cash machines and a pharmacy, and the standard first acclimatization stop.
tip: Spend two nights here. A day walk to the ridge above town does more for acclimatization than resting in the lodge.

name: Everest View Hotel
blurb: A hotel terrace on the Syangboche ridge above Namche with a clear line of sight to Everest, Lhotse and Ama Dablam. It is the usual target for the Namche acclimatization day.

name: Khumjung
blurb: A large Sherpa farming village beneath Khumbila, home to the school Edmund Hillary founded in 1961 and a monastery. Quieter than Namche and a good detour on the acclimatization day.

name: Tengboche
blurb: A ridge-top clearing with the largest monastery in Khumbu and a wide view of Ama Dablam, Everest and Lhotse. Lodges fill early in peak season.
tip: Visitors are normally welcome at the afternoon prayer session; dress warmly and stay quiet.

name: Pangboche
blurb: The highest year-round village on the Everest trail, with the oldest monastery in Khumbu in its upper half. The starting point for the side trip to Ama Dablam Base Camp.

name: Dingboche
blurb: A sunny summer settlement of stone-walled potato fields in the Imja valley and the usual second acclimatization stop. Sunnier and a little less windy than Pheriche next door.
tip: Take the rest day seriously: this is where most altitude problems on the Everest trail first show up.

name: Nangkartshang Peak
blurb: The steep ridge directly above Dingboche, climbed as an acclimatization hike. From the prayer flags you look across to Makalu, Lhotse, Island Peak and Ama Dablam.
tip: You do not have to reach the top; turning round at 4,800 m still gives your body the stimulus.

name: Pheriche
blurb: A windy valley-floor village with the Himalayan Rescue Association aid post, staffed by volunteer doctors in the main seasons. Most groups pass through on the way down.
tip: The aid post gives a free daily altitude talk in season. It is worth the hour.

name: Thukla
blurb: A pair of lodges at the snout of the Khumbu Glacier, where the trails from Dingboche and Pheriche meet. The climb above leads to a ridge of memorials to climbers who died on Everest.

name: Lobuche
blurb: A cold cluster of lodges beside the Khumbu Glacier moraine and the last overnight stop before Gorak Shep. Nights here are where many trekkers first sleep badly.

name: Gorak Shep
blurb: A handful of lodges on a frozen lakebed, the highest place to sleep on the trek and the base for both Everest Base Camp and Kala Patthar. Water is scarce and everything is expensive.
tip: One night is enough for most people. If you have a strong headache here, go down rather than waiting for morning.

name: Everest Base Camp
blurb: The south-side expedition base on the Khumbu Glacier, below the icefall. In April and May it is a tent city; the rest of the year it is bare moraine with a marker rock. Everest's summit is hidden from here.

name: Kala Patthar
blurb: A dark rocky shoulder of Pumori above Gorak Shep and the classic viewpoint for Everest, Nuptse and the Khumbu Icefall. Usually quoted at 5,545 m; surveys of the upper rocks put them about 100 m higher.
tip: Sunrise is very cold and the light on Everest is behind the peak; late afternoon gives better colour if the sky is clear.

name: Chheplung
blurb: A village half an hour north of Lukla where the old trail from Jiri and the Solu road-heads meets the main Everest trail. Walkers coming up from Surke join here and never need to enter Lukla.

name: Kyangjuma
blurb: A short row of lodges and jewellery stalls on the balcony trail east of Namche, just before the Sanasa junction where the Gokyo and Khumjung paths leave the main Everest trail. A sunny tea stop with Ama Dablam straight ahead.

name: Syangboche
blurb: A dirt airstrip on the shelf directly above Namche, used today by helicopters and the occasional cargo flight. The acclimatization paths to the Everest View Hotel, Khumjung and Khunde all cross it.

name: Khunde
blurb: Khumjung's quieter twin on the same high shelf, known for the hospital that Edmund Hillary's Himalayan Trust opened in 1966. It remains the main medical centre for the villages of upper Khumbu.

name: Phunki Tenga
blurb: The low point between Namche and Tengboche: a bridge over the Dudh Koshi, a row of water-driven prayer wheels and a few lunch lodges in the forest. The 600 m climb to the monastery starts on the far side.

name: Deboche
blurb: A quiet group of lodges in rhododendron and birch forest twenty minutes below Tengboche, next to a small nunnery. Groups sleep here when Tengboche is full, or for a less windy night.

name: Ama Dablam Base Camp
blurb: A broad grassy flat beneath the west face of Ama Dablam, about three hours' walk from Pangboche. In October and November it fills with expedition tents; for the rest of the year it is empty yak pasture.
tip: Carry lunch and at least two litres of water from Pangboche; do not count on finding food at base camp.

name: Chhukung
blurb: The last lodges in the Imja valley, on a gravel flat between the moraines of the Lhotse and Nuptse glaciers. It is the base for Chhukung Ri, the Kongma La and Island Peak, and climbing gear for the peak can be hired here.

name: Chhukung Ri
blurb: A rocky ridge above Chhukung with a close view of the south wall of Lhotse, Island Peak, Makalu and the north side of Ama Dablam. A steep, non-technical climb of about 800 m, used as the acclimatization hike before the Kongma La.
tip: The lower top at roughly 5,400 m is enough for most people; the last ridge to the true summit is loose and exposed.

name: Island Peak Base Camp
blurb: A dusty camping ground beside the Imja Glacier moraine, two to three hours beyond Chhukung. Trekkers walk up for the day; climbers sleep here before the pre-dawn start on Island Peak (Imja Tse).

name: Kongma La
blurb: The highest and roughest of the three passes, a rocky notch above a group of small lakes between Chhukung and Lobuche. There is no lodge, shelter or reliable water between the two villages.
tip: Leave Chhukung by six; the Khumbu Glacier crossing at the end of the day is slow and hard to follow in cloud.

name: Dzongla
blurb: A few lodges on a shelf under the north face of Cholatse, used the night before or after the Cho La. Beds are limited and run short when bad weather has held groups back for a day.

name: Cho La
blurb: The pass between the Khumbu and Gokyo valleys. The east side crosses a short stretch of snow-covered glacier and the west side is a steep slope of loose rock, so it needs more care than its height alone suggests.
tip: Carry microspikes, cross early in the day and do not start up in fresh snow or thick cloud.

name: Thagnak
blurb: A handful of lodges in a sheltered side valley on the east edge of the Ngozumpa Glacier, two to three hours from Gokyo. It is the staging point for the Cho La on the Gokyo side.

name: Mong La
blurb: A chorten and a row of tea houses on a spur of Khumbila, high above the Dudh Koshi. The Gokyo trail crosses it between the Sanasa junction and the steep drop to Phortse Tenga.

name: Phortse Tenga
blurb: A few lodges in birch and rhododendron forest beside the Dudh Koshi, at the bottom of the descent from Mong La. A bridge leads across and up to Phortse; the Gokyo trail stays on the west bank.

name: Phortse
blurb: A farming village on a shelf above the meeting of the Dudh Koshi and the Imja Khola, home to many Everest climbing Sherpas and to the Khumbu Climbing Center. It lies off the main trail, so evenings are quiet.

name: Dole
blurb: The first lodges above the forest in the Gokyo valley, in a stream gully facing Kangtega and Thamserku. It is 600 m higher than Namche, and many people first feel the altitude here.

name: Machhermo
blurb: A lodge settlement in a side valley under Machhermo Peak and the usual last night before Gokyo. A porter shelter and rescue post with volunteer medics has operated here in the main trekking seasons.
tip: If you arrive with a headache, stay a second night rather than moving up to the lakes.

name: Gokyo
blurb: A lodge village on the shore of the third Gokyo lake, Dudh Pokhari, with the Ngozumpa Glacier hidden behind the moraine at its back. It is the base for Gokyo Ri, the upper lakes, the Renjo La and the Cho La.
tip: Give it two nights. Gokyo Ri is far harder the morning after you arrive than after a day at this height.

name: Gokyo Ri
blurb: The brown hill above Gokyo, a steady two to three hour climb from the lake shore. From the top you see Everest, Lhotse, Makalu and Cho Oyu at once, with the Ngozumpa Glacier and the lakes spread out below.
tip: Cloud often fills the valley by late morning; go up at dawn or, on a settled day, for the evening light on Everest.

name: Gokyo Fourth Lake
blurb: Thonak Tsho, the largest and deepest of the Gokyo lakes, an hour or so beyond the village on the level trail between the moraine and the hillside. A sensible turnaround if the fifth lake is too far.

name: Gokyo Fifth Lake
blurb: Ngozumpa Tsho, two and a half to three hours north of Gokyo. The moraine crest beside it, known as Scoundrel's Viewpoint, looks up the glacier to Cho Oyu and across to Everest, with more of the mountain showing than from Gokyo Ri.
tip: Nothing is sold beyond Gokyo; take lunch, water and a windproof layer.

name: Renjo La
blurb: The westernmost of the three passes, between Gokyo and the Thame valley. A built stone staircase covers the steepest ground on the west side, and the view east from the top takes in Everest, Lhotse and Makalu above the Gokyo lake.

name: Lungden
blurb: A small group of lodges in the upper Bhote Koshi valley and the first shelter west of the Renjo La. The valley continues north to the Nangpa La, the old trade route into Tibet.

name: Thame
blurb: A village of scattered stone houses at the mouth of the Thame valley, with a monastery on the cliff above. A glacial lake flood in August 2024 destroyed many houses and lodges on the lower ground, and rebuilding has been under way since.
tip: Confirm in Namche which lodges are open before you plan a night here.

name: Thamo
blurb: A village on the trail between Namche and Thame with a nunnery and the small hydropower station that supplies electricity to Namche and the surrounding villages.

name: Jiri
blurb: A bazaar town in Dolakha district, about 190 km by road from Kathmandu. From the 1980s, when the Swiss-built road reached it, until Lukla flights became routine, the walk to Everest began here. Buses now carry on to Shivalaya.

name: Shivalaya
blurb: A single street of lodges beside the Khimti Khola, and the place where most people on the Jiri route now start walking. The Gaurishankar Conservation Area checkpost at the end of the village checks or sells the permit.

name: Deurali (Bhandar)
blurb: A forested pass with long mani walls and a few lodges between Shivalaya and Bhandar. It is the first real climb of the Jiri trail, about 900 m above the Khimti Khola, with Bhandar's fields in view on the far side.

name: Bhandar
blurb: A spread-out Sherpa village on a wide shelf, with two large stupas and a small monastery at its centre. A rough road now reaches it, and in the dry months jeeps from Kathmandu or Jiri use it as a starting point.

name: Kinja
blurb: A warm riverside bazaar where the Kinja Khola meets the Likhu Khola. It is the low point before the Lamjura La: from here the trail climbs 1,900 m to the pass.

name: Sete
blurb: A few lodges and a small monastery on the steep ridge above Kinja, roughly halfway up the long climb to the Lamjura La. Stopping here splits the ascent into two manageable days.

name: Lamjura La
blurb: The highest point between Jiri and Namche, a forested pass crossed on stone steps through rhododendron and fir. Snow and ice can lie on the trail from December to March, and cloud usually closes in by midday.

name: Junbesi
blurb: A well-kept Sherpa village around an old monastery in the upper Solu valley, with comfortable lodges, apple orchards and a school built by Hillary's Himalayan Trust. A good place to spend a rest day.

name: Taksindu La
blurb: A pass marked by a large white stupa on the ridge between the Solu valley and the Dudh Koshi. The monastery of the same name lies just below on the east side, and the descent to Nunthala is long and stony.

name: Nunthala
blurb: A roadside village of lodges on the long slope between the Taksindu La and the Dudh Koshi. Maps and itineraries quote its height anywhere from about 2,200 to 2,350 m.

name: Jubing
blurb: A Rai farming village among terraces of maize and millet just above the Dudh Koshi bridge. This is the lowest and warmest stretch of the walk-in from Jiri.

name: Kharikhola
blurb: A long village of Magar and Sherpa houses strung along a ridge above the Dudh Koshi. Jeeps from Salleri now reach it, which makes it one of the usual starting points for people walking in from the road.

name: Bupsa
blurb: Lodges and a small monastery on a ridge about an hour and a half above the Khari Khola stream, looking back down the valley. A night here takes the first 400 m out of the climb toward Paiya.

name: Paiya
blurb: A lodge stop in forest on the hillside south of Lukla, between the Kari La shoulder and the Chutok La. In recent seasons the jeep track from the south has ended at Thamdanda, a short walk before Paiya; ask where it stops now.

name: Chutok La
blurb: A low forested pass between Paiya and Surke and the last climb of the walk-in before the trail drops into the valley below Lukla. The path is narrow and shared with mule trains.
tip: Stand on the uphill side when mules pass; the drop on the outer edge is steep.

name: Surke
blurb: A few lodges in a damp side valley directly below Lukla. One trail climbs steeply from here to the airstrip; another continues north through Chaurikharka to Chheplung and joins the main Everest trail without entering Lukla.

name: Dhap
blurb: A roadside bazaar on the Okhaldhunga to Salleri road at the southern edge of Solukhumbu, and the usual start of the Pikey Peak trek. Jeeps from Kathmandu take most of a day to reach it.

name: Jhapre
blurb: A ridge-top village with a small monastery and a stupa, and a first clear look north to Everest and the Numbur range. It is the normal first night on the walk from Dhap.

name: Pikey Base Camp
blurb: A handful of basic lodges on open yak pasture below the summit ridge, where trekkers sleep before the dawn climb. It is exposed and cold at night, and water is scarce in the dry months.
tip: Rooms are few; in October, November and April have someone phone ahead from Jhapre.

name: Pikey Peak
blurb: The highest point of the lower Solu ridges, a grassy twin summit strung with prayer flags. On a clear morning the view runs from Gaurishankar and Numbur past Everest and Makalu to Kanchenjunga on the eastern horizon.
tip: Be on top at sunrise; haze and cloud usually build from mid-morning.

name: Jase Bhanjyang
blurb: A saddle with two or three lodges on the north side of Pikey Peak, where the summit trail meets the routes down to Junbesi and Loding. Some groups sleep here after the summit instead of pushing on.

name: Thupten Chholing
blurb: A large Tibetan Buddhist monastery about an hour and a half up the valley from Junbesi, founded by Trulshik Rinpoche in the 1960s. Several hundred monks and nuns live in the small houses on the hillside around it.
tip: Dress modestly, ask before taking photographs and leave a small donation.

name: Phaplu
blurb: A small town with an airstrip and a hospital, just up the road from the district headquarters at Salleri. Jeeps for Kathmandu leave before dawn, and it is the usual end of the Pikey Peak trek.

name: Salleri
blurb: The district headquarters of Solukhumbu, strung along the road below Phaplu. It has banks, a weekly market and the jeep stand for Kathmandu and for the road-heads further north toward Lukla.
